summary: The plan has a genuinely good shape at the service and handler layers — the US-13 grant test asserts on repository state and not just the status code, which is the single most important thing this feature needed, and Task 2's mailpit smoke check is real verification. But the plan is truncated at both ends: the production persistence layer (PostgresRepository/GORM against MariaDB) and the entire client half of the feature have zero automated coverage, and several service-level unit tests assert invariants that live in the stub rather than in the code under test. Three of the tech-spec's own Acceptance Criteria have no test and no AVP step. The 'no live-MariaDB tests' and 'no CI job' exclusions are stated as facts about the current repo rather than argued as trade-offs, and both are cheaper to fix than the spec implies: docker-compose.yml already publishes mariadb:11.4 on host port 3306, migrations.Run(*sql.DB) is an exported function taking a plain *sql.DB, and .github/workflows/deploy.yml is an existing workflow that a `go test ./...` step could join in ~8 lines.

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy > Integration tests; Task 4
findings.description: PostgresRepository — the storage used in production (APP_STORAGE=mysql) — gets no automated test at any level. access_repo_test.go is scoped to MemoryRepository, and every handler test also runs on MemoryRepository. So the GORM/SQL implementations of EnsureUser, GetUser, ListUsers, SetAccess, CreateRequest, GetRequest and DecideRequest written in Task 4 are verified by nothing but one manual curl walkthrough. This includes GetUser, which is the read that RequireAdmin bases its authorization decision on, and SetAccess, which is the write that US-13 protects. Today userModel (server/internal/repository/postgres.go:15-18) has only ID and CreatedAt; Task 4 must add Role/HasAccess/Email gorm tags. A wrong or missing column tag makes role scan as empty on every request — RequireAdmin then either locks both admins out or, depending on how the check is written, fails open — and no test in this plan fails. The AVP itself admits dev compose defaults to MemoryRepository because APP_STORAGE is unset, so even the manual walkthrough exercises the DB path only if the agent remembers one env var.
findings.recommendation: Write access_repo_test.go as a shared contract function rather than a memory-only test: `func runUserRepositoryContract(t *testing.T, newRepo func(t *testing.T) service.UserRepository)`, containing the invariants the service depends on. Run it twice — once with NewMemoryRepository, once with NewPostgresRepository over a live DSN. Gate the second with `dsn := os.Getenv("TEST_DB_DSN"); if dsn == "" { t.Skip("TEST_DB_DSN not set") }` so the suite stays green with no DB present. Setup is small because migrations.Run(db *sql.DB) is already exported and docker-compose.yml already publishes mariadb:11.4 on 3306: open the DSN, run migrations.Run, truncate access_requests/users per test. Minimum assertions on the live run: after EnsureUser(login,email) a users row exists with role='user' and has_access=0; a second EnsureUser with a different email leaves role and has_access untouched (see the admin-demotion finding); SetAccess(login,true) then GetUser returns HasAccess==true and Role unchanged; SetAccess on an unknown login returns ErrNotFound and inserts no row; GetUser on a row with role='admin' returns Role=="admin" (this is the authorization read — assert it against a real column, not a fake).

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy > Unit tests, bullet 'EnsureUser для существующего пользователя не сбрасывает role и has_access'
findings.description: Litmus test failure on the admin-demotion path. AccessService.EnsureUser almost certainly just forwards to repo.EnsureUser — there is no service-level logic to make idempotent. The non-overwrite invariant lives entirely in the SQL (INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, or GORM FirstOrCreate vs Save/Assign). A unit test on a hand-written stub therefore asserts that the test author's own stub does not overwrite — remove the service body entirely and the test still passes. Meanwhile the real failure mode is severe and silent: if the Postgres implementation uses GORM Save or Assign, every login rewrites the row and resets role to the 'user' default, demoting both administrators the next time they sign in and leaving nobody able to grant access. Decision 11 calls EnsureUser on every login, so this fires on the very first admin login after deploy. Nothing in this plan tests it. The same pattern weakens the 'SetAccess(granted=true) выставляет флаг' and 'SetAccess(granted=false) снимает флаг' bullets: if the service forwards to the repo, those assert stub behavior too.
findings.recommendation: Move the idempotency invariant into the repository contract suite (previous finding) where it can run against real SQL, and assert it as state: EnsureUser('ivan',''), then SetAccess('ivan',true) and a direct role='admin' update, then EnsureUser('ivan','new@ya.ru') again, then GetUser('ivan') must still return Role=='admin' and HasAccess==true — only Email may change. Keep a service-level test only where the service actually decides something: the has_access||role=='admin' override (Decision 10), the 409 rules, and mapping unknown login to ErrNotFound. For SetAccess, make the service test earn its place by asserting the coordination the service really owns — that SetAccess(true) results in both the flag set AND DecideRequest called with status 'approved' and decided_by equal to the calling admin's login, read back off the stub's recorded arguments, not just that the flag is true.

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy; Task 5 (Files to modify lists no test file)
findings.description: Task 5 creates the entire session-identity mechanism — new columns written by auth.Store.CreateSession, read by FindByRefreshHash, and rotated by HandleRefresh via UpdateSessionTokens — and its Files to modify list contains no test file at all. The Testing Strategy compensates by stubbing the session resolver in every handler test, which is the right call for the handler tests but leaves the store itself with zero coverage. Two silent, high-impact failure modes go untested: (a) if the INSERT in CreateSession or the SELECT in FindByRefreshHash omits the new yandex_login column, every user permanently gets session_identity_missing and the entire feature is dead on arrival for everyone, not just pre-migration sessions; (b) worse, Decision 1 requires identity to survive token rotation, and UpdateSessionTokens (server/internal/auth/store.go) currently rewrites the session row — if its UPDATE does not preserve or re-set yandex_login, users lose their identity roughly one access-token lifetime after login, which is a delayed failure that a fresh-login manual walkthrough will never reproduce. There is no test and no AVP step for rotation preserving identity.
findings.recommendation: Add auth/store_test.go to Task 5, gated on TEST_DB_DSN with t.Skip like the repository contract suite, asserting round-trips rather than mocks: CreateSession with YandexLogin='ivan'/YandexEmail='i@ya.ru' then FindByRefreshHash returns both fields intact; a session created before the migration (INSERT leaving both columns NULL) round-trips as a valid Session with an empty login and does not error on Scan — this is exactly Decision 2's contract and sql.NullString handling is where it will break; and, most importantly, CreateSession then UpdateSessionTokens with a rotated hash, then FindByRefreshHash on the new hash still returns YandexLogin=='ivan'. Add a matching AVP step: log in, force a refresh via POST /auth/refresh, then call GET /api/v1/access/me and assert it still returns the login rather than 401 session_identity_missing.

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy (no client subsection); Tasks 7 and 8
findings.description: The client half of the feature has no tests, no test infrastructure, and no plan to add either. client/package.json has no test runner, no test script, and no testing devDependencies; there are no .test.jsx files anywhere in the repo. The Testing Strategy section never mentions the client at all — it does not even declare 'None' with a reason, it simply omits it, while the E2E subsection's 'None' addresses only Playwright/Cypress. Yet US-1, US-2, US-4, US-7, US-8, US-11 and US-12 are all client-side criteria, and Tasks 7 and 8 both list test-reviewer as a reviewer for code that will ship with zero tests. Concretely unprotected: the Panel.jsx status machine's new no-access branch, and the effect guards that stop a user without access from fetching /settings and /chats. That guard is a regression waiting to happen — the risks table itself notes the effects are keyed on profile rather than status — and the tech-spec's own acceptance criterion for it is verified only by a human reading the browser Network tab once. The E2E exclusion is defensible on cost; the total absence of any client test is a separate decision the spec never actually makes or justifies.
findings.recommendation: Either state and own the consequence explicitly in the Testing Strategy ('client code ships with no regression protection; all client criteria are verified once, manually, per deploy'), or add the cheap middle option the spec skipped: vitest + jsdom + @testing-library/react is a devDependency install and a four-line vite config, with no CI or browser required. Highest-value first, as three small component tests: render Panel with a stubbed accessApi returning {has_access:false, role:'user'} and assert the request banner is present, the working interface is absent, and — the regression-prone one — that the injected fetch/panelApi stub was never called with /settings or /chats; render with {has_access:false, role:'admin'} and assert the working interface and the Пользователи nav item both render, covering Decision 10 in the UI; render with {has_access:true, role:'user'} and assert the Пользователи nav item is absent, which is the only real assertion of US-12 anywhere in this plan. Add these to Tasks 7 and 8 as Files to modify, otherwise the test-reviewer on both tasks has nothing to review.

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy > Integration tests, bullet 'GET /api/v1/admin/users неадминистратором → 403 (US-12)'; Agent Verification Plan item 3
findings.description: US-12 is mis-mapped, which inflates apparent coverage of a criterion flagged as security-critical. US-12 reads 'Пользователь без прав администратора не видит раздел управления пользователями' — a UI-visibility criterion. The API returning 403 is US-13's concern and is already claimed by US-13 elsewhere in the same list. Tagging the 403 test with US-12 makes the traceability matrix look complete while nothing in the Testing Strategy or the AVP actually verifies that a non-admin does not see the section: AVP item 3 enumerates three states but for the admin state asserts only that Пользователи IS visible, and never asserts the negative for the ordinary user. The only place the negative appears in the whole tech-spec is one clause at the end of Task 8's Verify-user line. Note that UI hiding is not itself a security control — the 403 is, and that is properly covered — but a stated acceptance criterion is being reported as tested by a test that does not test it.
findings.recommendation: Remove the (US-12) tag from the admin-users 403 bullet and label that bullet (US-13) alongside the grant test. Cover US-12 with the client render test described above (role:'user' → Пользователи nav item absent). Add the negative to AVP item 3 explicitly: 'пользователь с доступом, role=user → рабочий интерфейс отображается И пункта «Пользователи» в навигации нет', so the AVP asserts both directions rather than only the admin-positive case.

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy (opening paragraph); Implementation Tasks (no task adds CI)
findings.description: The 'no CI job' exclusion is not justified — it is circular and it is the cheapest fix in the plan. .github/workflows/deploy.yml exists and contains no test invocation, so today nothing runs costing_test.go automatically either, and after this feature nothing will run the ~30 new tests either. The tech-spec lists 'Все существующие тесты проходят; регрессий в costing_test.go нет' as an acceptance criterion with no enforcement mechanism whatsoever — it is satisfied only by whoever remembers to type go test ./... before merging. The Testing Strategy then uses the absence of a CI job as part of its justification for excluding live-DB tests, which reasons from a gap to excuse a second gap. Every unit and httptest test in this plan is hermetic: no DB, no network, no secrets, no services. No Implementation Task covers this — Task 9 is the deploy task and its scope is env vars and nginx proxying.
findings.recommendation: Add a test job to the existing workflow and a line item to Task 9 (or a new small task): a job with actions/setup-go@v5 at go 1.25.5 running `go test ./...` in ./server, made a needs: dependency of build-and-deploy so a red suite blocks the deploy. That is roughly eight lines and no new infrastructure. If the live-DB contract run from the first finding is adopted, add `services: mariadb:11.4` to that job and set TEST_DB_DSN — GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runners support service containers natively, so this needs no self-hosted runner and no new secrets. Without this job, every finding fixed in this review decays silently on the next unrelated change.

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy > Integration tests, bullet 'POST /api/v1/admin/users/{login}/access неадминистратором → 403 и флаг в репозитории не изменился'
findings.description: This is the strongest bullet in the plan — asserting on repository state rather than the status code alone is exactly right for US-13, and it should be kept as written. But it covers only one of the three cases US-13 names. US-13 says verbatim 'Неадминистратор не может выдать доступ никому, включая себя' and the self-grant case — the actual attack a motivated user attempts — is not in the test list and not in the AVP, which likewise says only 'попытка выдать доступ неадминистратором' without specifying the target. Self-targeting is a distinct code path in any implementation that special-cases the caller, and it is one line of test. Two further gaps in the same area: there is no unauthenticated case for this endpoint (the list has 'GET /api/v1/admin/users без кук → 401' but no POST equivalent, so a missing RequireAuth on the write route would be caught only by Task 6's smoke curl, not by any test), and the state assertion is attached only to the 403 case, not to the 404 unknown-login case, so a handler that creates the target row before checking its existence would pass.
findings.recommendation: Split into three bullets, each keeping the state assertion. (1) Non-admin 'ivan' POSTs {granted:true} to /api/v1/admin/users/ivan/access — his own login — expect 403 AND repo.GetUser('ivan').HasAccess still false AND Role still 'user'. (2) Non-admin 'ivan' targets 'petr' — expect 403 AND GetUser('petr').HasAccess unchanged (the bullet as currently written). (3) No cookies at all — expect 401 AND the target's flag unchanged. Add to the 404 bullet: AND ListUsers() length is unchanged, so no row was created for the unknown login. Update AVP step 2 to name the self-grant explicitly, since that is the wording the user-spec criterion uses.

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy > Unit tests > notifier_test.go, bullets 'Тема письма...' and 'Тело письма содержит логин и email заявителя'
findings.description: The notifier tests are structure-shaped, not behavior-shaped. 'Тело письма содержит логин и email заявителя' is a substring-presence assertion — it passes on a message that is nothing but the login and email concatenated, with no headers, no CRLF separator between headers and body, and no valid RFC 5322 structure. Substring presence verifies that a string appears, not that the artifact behaves correctly. The bugs that actually occur when hand-rolling net/smtp messages — a missing blank line between headers and body, an un-encoded 8-bit Subject, a malformed To list — all survive these assertions. More seriously, there is no test for header injection, which is the classic net/smtp vulnerability: the message is built from a Yandex login and email, and if either contains CRLF an attacker can inject arbitrary headers (Bcc, a forged From) into mail sent to both administrators. net/smtp performs no sanitization. security-auditor is listed as a reviewer on Task 2 but the test plan gives it nothing to verify.
findings.recommendation: Replace substring checks with a round-trip parse. Build the message, parse it with net/mail.ReadMessage, then assert: mime.WordDecoder{}.DecodeHeader(msg.Header.Get("Subject")) equals the exact expected Russian subject (this proves both the RFC 2047 encoding and that headers and body are correctly separated — an unparseable message fails here rather than silently passing a Contains check); msg.Header.Get("To") equals the configured admin list; and the body read from msg.Body equals the expected rendered text for a known login/email pair. Add the injection case: build a message for login "ivan\r\nBcc: attacker@evil.com" and assert either that construction returns an error, or that the parsed message has no Bcc header and the login appears only in the body with control characters stripped. For the no-email case, assert on the parsed body's exact content rather than on the absence of a substring.

findings.location: Section: Acceptance Criteria, items 'Ошибка отправки письма не влияет на код ответа при создании заявки' and 'При незаданном SMTP_HOST сервер стартует... заявки создаются'
findings.description: Two acceptance criteria have no test in the Testing Strategy and no step in the AVP. They are also the two that encode a hard user-spec constraint ('сбой отправки письма не должен ронять создание заявки') and a listed user-spec risk. The Testing Strategy's only notifier-availability bullet is 'Нотификатор с пустым SMTP_HOST не конструируется (возвращает nil)', which tests the constructor in isolation and says nothing about the handler's behavior when the notifier is nil or when SendMail fails — and the nil case is a live nil-pointer risk at the call site, since Decision 7 has the handler invoke the notifier from a goroutine. The handler test list contains 'POST /api/v1/access/requests дважды подряд → 201, затем 409' but never exercises a failing or absent notifier. Both of these are pure handler tests requiring no SMTP server.
findings.recommendation: Make the notifier an interface at the handler boundary so it can be substituted, then add two handler tests. (1) Notifier stub whose Send always returns an error: POST /api/v1/access/requests still returns 201 AND repo.GetRequest(login).Status == 'pending' — the request must be durably created despite the failure. (2) Notifier is nil (SMTP_HOST unset): the same POST returns 201, the request exists, and the handler does not panic. Both are also the natural place to fix the flakiness hazard noted separately: give the stub a buffered channel and have the test select on it with a short timeout so the assertion is deterministic rather than racing the fire-and-forget goroutine.

findings.location: Section: Acceptance Criteria, item 'Ответ 500 из нового контура не содержит текста внутренней ошибки'; Section: Risks
findings.description: An acceptance criterion with zero verification anywhere. The risks table correctly identifies that writeAPIDomainError's default branch passes err.Error() straight to the client (confirmed at server/internal/handler/http.go, default case calls writeAPIError with err.Error()) and states the mitigation that the new contour's 500 branch returns fixed text. But there is no test for it in the Testing Strategy, no AVP step, and no smoke check in Task 5 or Task 6. A mitigation that nothing verifies is a plan, not a control — and the leak this guards against is a DSN or SQL fragment reaching an unauthenticated caller, since the 500 path is reachable before any authorization succeeds. The handler test list does cover the 400/401/403/404/409 branches but stops short of 500, which is the only one with a disclosure consequence.
findings.recommendation: Add a handler test with a repository stub whose GetUser returns a raw error carrying a recognizable secret-shaped string (e.g. errors.New("dial tcp 10.0.0.5:3306: connection refused, user=poshivon password=poshivon")): call GET /api/v1/access/me with a valid stubbed session, assert the status is 500 AND that the response body does not contain "password", "3306", or the raw error text, AND that it equals the fixed payload the contour is supposed to return, e.g. {"error":"internal_error"}. Assert on the exact expected body rather than only on absence, so the test also pins the contract instead of passing on an empty response.

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy > Integration tests, 'server/internal/repository/access_repo_test.go — контрактные тесты на MemoryRepository'
findings.description: A contract test suite that runs against exactly one of the two implementations is not a contract test — it is a unit test of the fake. The spec names these 'контрактные тесты, проверяющие те же инварианты, что ожидает сервис' while structurally guaranteeing that the implementation the service actually runs against in production is never checked against those invariants. This is the specific mechanism by which the two implementations will drift: MemoryRepository is written by the same task, in the same session, to satisfy the same tests, so it will agree with the service by construction, while PostgresRepository agrees with nothing. The compile-time assertions listed in the acceptance criteria only prove that both types satisfy the interface signatures, not that they behave alike.
findings.recommendation: Restructure as a table of implementations rather than a memory-only file: define the suite once as a function taking a factory, then range over the implementations under test, skipping the SQL one when TEST_DB_DSN is unset. This is a small structural change that costs nothing today and makes closing the PostgresRepository gap a matter of setting one environment variable rather than writing a second suite. Invariants the suite must pin for both: EnsureUser is idempotent and never downgrades role or has_access; GetUser on an absent login returns ErrNotFound rather than a zero-value record with an empty role (a zero-value return here is what turns a missing user into a silent non-admin instead of an error); ListUsers returns every user created via EnsureUser including those who never submitted a request; CreateRequest on an existing pending row surfaces the conflict rather than silently overwriting; DecideRequest sets status, decided_by and decided_at together.

findings.description: The tests filed under 'Integration tests' integrate with nothing external: httptest recorder plus MemoryRepository plus a stubbed session resolver is a wide unit test of the handler layer. That is a perfectly good and appropriate test type — the objection is to the label, because the label is doing argumentative work. Presenting these as the integration tier is what makes the subsequent exclusion of live-MariaDB tests read as reasonable ('integration is already covered'), when in fact no test in the plan crosses a process boundary, touches SQL, or exercises real cookie/session handling. The user-spec's Testing section asked for integration tests specifically because 'проверка доступа и админских операций затрагивает БД' — the DB is precisely what these do not touch.
findings.recommendation: Rename the subsection to 'Handler tests (httptest + in-memory)' and add a one-line honest statement of what tier is missing and why, so reviewers price the exclusion correctly: 'Тестов, пересекающих границу процесса, в наборе нет; SQL-слой проверяется только вручную через AVP.' If the gated live-DB contract run from the earlier findings is adopted, that becomes the real integration tier and this subsection can keep its accurate narrower name.

findings.location: Decision 7; Section: Testing Strategy > Integration tests
findings.description: Decision 7 sends the admin notification from a bare goroutine launched after the request is created. Any handler test for POST /api/v1/access/requests will therefore return while that goroutine is still running, which produces a test that is nondeterministic under -race and can log or panic after the test function has completed. The plan does not mention any synchronization point, and there is no mechanism in the design (no WaitGroup, no injectable done-channel) that a test could wait on.
findings.recommendation: Give the notifier call an injectable seam so tests are deterministic: have AccessHandler hold a notifier interface and, in tests, use a stub that signals a buffered channel on Send; the test then selects on that channel with a 1-second timeout before asserting. This also lets the test assert what was sent — that Send received the requesting user's login and email — turning a fire-and-forget side effect into verified behavior. Run the suite with -race in the CI job so this class of problem surfaces.

findings.description: The AVP curl scenario drops a step the user-spec's How to Verify table contains. The user-spec lists step 6, 'Отозвать доступ под администратором → 204, флаг доступа в БД снят', but AVP item 2's scenario runs only отсутствие доступа → подача заявки → повторная подача (409) → выдача доступа → проверка состояния, and stops there. Revocation is the operation US-10 depends on, it is the one the user-spec risks section worries about most, and against a real DB it is the write most likely to differ from the grant path (a SetAccess implementation using a non-zero-value-safe GORM Updates call will silently no-op on granted=false, since false is Go's zero value — a bug class that the memory implementation cannot reproduce).
findings.recommendation: Extend AVP item 2 with the revoke step and a DB read-back: after granting, POST {"granted":false} as the admin, expect 204, then confirm via docker exec mariadb -e "SELECT has_access FROM users WHERE id='...'" that the value is 0, and confirm GET /api/v1/access/me for that user now reports has_access:false. Given the GORM zero-value pitfall, also add the granted=false round-trip explicitly to the repository contract suite so it is caught by a test rather than only by the one-shot walkthrough.

findings.location: Section: Acceptance Criteria, item 'Строка users появляется после входа, до каких-либо действий в панели'
findings.description: This criterion has no owner. It cannot be exercised by the agent, since it requires a real Yandex OAuth login that the AVP cannot perform headlessly, and it is not listed under User verifies in the user-spec either. It is a genuinely important criterion — Decision 11 exists specifically because without it the admin list is empty for exactly the users the feature is for, and the access_requests foreign key has nothing to point at — so leaving it unassigned means the central premise of Decision 11 is confirmed by nobody.
findings.recommendation: Cover the mechanism where it is testable and assign the rest explicitly. At the handler level, the login path calls AccessService.EnsureUser after session creation: add a test that after the login handler runs successfully, repo.ListUsers() contains the new login with has_access=false and role='user', with no settings, chats or calculations having been written. Then add the live confirmation to the post-deploy task (Task 15) as a user-verified item: after an admin's first real login, SELECT id, role, has_access FROM users returns the row, which is also the prerequisite for the manual admin UPDATE described in Data Models.

metrics.pyramidNote: Not inverted — truncated. A solid service-level base and a reasonable handler tier sit over an empty persistence foundation (zero tests touch MariaDB/GORM, the production storage) and an empty top (zero client tests, zero E2E). The 16 counted as integration are httptest + in-memory + stubbed session resolver, i.e. wide unit tests; no test in the plan crosses a process boundary.
